title: Candid homepage: grants and nonprofit data with AI donor note
answer: This is the Candid homepage, a landing page from Candid, a provider of grants and nonprofit data. It says Candid offers comprehensive grants and nonprofit data to help users find funding, research nonprofits, connect with funders and more. The most useful point for AI readers is a short note that donors increasingly use AI tools to research causes and charities, so many will not ever see a nonprofit's website, donation page or newsletter. The page gives little detail beyond these statements.

sections.body: Candid publishes this page. It is a landing page or homepage for Candid, described as providing grants and nonprofit data. Its stated scope is finding funding, researching nonprofits and connecting with funders. The harvested text does not state a publication or update date. It is a short landing page rather than a report, article or dataset.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents Candid as a source of grants and nonprofit data. It repeats its main description twice, saying Candid provides the most comprehensive grants and nonprofit data to help you find funding, research nonprofits, connect with funders and more. The only other substantive sentence is about AI. It says donors are increasingly using AI tools to research causes and charities. Because of this, it says, many donors will not ever see your nonprofit's website, donation page or newsletter. The text does not explain which AI tools are used, how donors use them, or what nonprofits should do in response. It does not give examples, statistics, dates or sources for the AI claim. It also does not describe specific grant programs, funding trends, technology infrastructure grants or AI adoption funding. The page is mostly a gateway to Candid's data and services, with the AI sentence standing as a brief observation for nonprofits.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numbers. It makes two notable claims. First, Candid provides the most comprehensive grants and nonprofit data. Second, donors are increasingly using AI tools to research causes and charities, which means many will not ever see a nonprofit's website, donation page or newsletter. The text does not define AI tools, quantify the trend or provide evidence for either claim.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in nonprofits would use this page mainly for the donor behavior claim. It suggests that AI mediated research may bypass nonprofit owned channels, so a website, donation page or newsletter may not be the first or only place donors encounter a cause. The page does not discuss AI adoption funding, technology infrastructure grants or grantmaking trends, so it is useful as a brief awareness signal rather than a detailed evidence source.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Nonprofits

sections.body: This is a landing page with little substance. It does not cover grantmaking trends, AI adoption funding, technology infrastructure, specific funders, grant amounts, dates or research methods. The AI statement is brief and unsourced. The text does not state a publication date. It appears to be a commercial page for Candid's data services, and the harvested text is partial, ending with an ellipsis after the AI sentence.
